description.value: A within-subject BOLD fMRI study examined smoking cue reactivity during smoking satiety and acute 24-hour abstinence and tested whether abstinence-induced ACC signal changes predicted short-term smoking relapse and days abstinent.

spans.text: This study evaluated the relationship between brain responses to smoking cues during acute abstinence (vs. satiety) and short-term relapse in 75 treatment-seeking smokers.

value: we hypothesized that heightened smoking cue reactivity during abstinence (relative to smoking satiety) in the attentional, cognitive control, and reward networks would predict the likelihood of short-term smoking relapse (biochemically confirmed in the first 7 days of a quit attempt).
